wordpressSecurity.seoTitle: WordPress Security Check & PHP Updates | CartShift Studio
wordpressSecurity.seoDescription: A careful WordPress security and updates review: verify PHP2Shell patch status, audit WordPress plugins and themes, check backups, and apply approved fixes with regression checks.
wordpressSecurity.title: Know where your WordPress site stands.
wordpressSecurity.subtitle: Recent critical PHP vulnerabilities are a timely reason to check your hosting. We verify what is actually patched, review WordPress maintenance risks, and make only the changes your site needs.
trustNotes: A real technical review, not an automated score
wordpressSecurity.alertText: On 21 October 2026, PHP released fixes for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. Vulnerable PHP installations may allow unauthenticated remote code execution. Not every WordPress site is still exposed: hosting providers may already have patched their servers.
wordpressSecurity.whyTitle: WordPress updates alone are not the PHP fix.
wordpressSecurity.whyText: These vulnerabilities are in the PHP runtime. Updating WordPress or installing a security plugin does not replace the PHP patch supplied by your server administrator or host. WordPress, plugins and themes still deserve a separate security and compatibility review.
wordpressSecurity.serviceTitle: A practical security check, from server to site
wordpressSecurity.serviceIntro: A defined, evidence-led review followed by approved, carefully scoped fixes.

wordpressSecurity.scopeTitle: A security review, without exaggerated promises
wordpressSecurity.scopeText: This is a targeted WordPress and PHP maintenance engagement—not a penetration test, malware incident response, forensic investigation or a guarantee that no vulnerability exists. Complex upgrades, breaches and custom fixes are scoped separately.

faq.question: Does every WordPress site have this PHP vulnerability?
faq.answer: No. Exposure depends on the PHP runtime and the hosting provider's patch status. Some providers ship backported fixes without changing the visible PHP version number, so we verify rather than guess.

faq.question: Will updating WordPress fix PHP2Shell?
faq.answer: No. The PHP vulnerabilities require a patched PHP runtime from the host or server administrator. WordPress and plugin updates address separate risks.

faq.question: Will you update all plugins automatically?
faq.answer: No. We first assess versions, compatibility and business-critical workflows. We back up before agreed updates and test afterward.

faq.question: Can you review my online store?
faq.answer: This specific service is for standard WordPress sites, such as business websites, magazines and content portals. WooCommerce stores are outside the scope of this offer.

faq.question: What will it cost?
faq.answer: We assess the site's scope and provide an estimate before beginning paid work. Unexpected or complex issues require a separate approval.
